prompt.intro: I'm reading an article about BIM and IFC files. Please help me understand this content better.
prompt.step1: Summarize the 3 most important practical takeaways in plain language
prompt.step2: Explain the technical terms (IFC entities, standards, acronyms) I might not know
prompt.step3: Give me one concrete action I should take based on this article
prompt.step4: Answer any follow-up questions I have on this topic
prompt.tail: If I give you a path to an IFC file or describe my project, relate your answers to my specific situation.

doc.footer: This article is from IFC Viewer Online — a free in-browser IFC viewer. Files never leave your machine. Try it at {{site}}

midBody.validation: I built the viewer so you can open an IFC and see its Health Score in a minute, locally. Validation Pro adds the full rule set and reports.
midBody.iso19650: Open your IFC and see where names and data break ISO 19650. The ISO 19650 checks in Team run that on every delivery.
midBody.steel: Profiles, lengths and weights grouped per profile, isolated in 3D and exported. Steel Takeoff does this on your own models.
midBody.large: The viewer opens big files in your browser. For federated sets of several models, I am building large-model federation in Pro.
midBody.twin: Your model is the base of the twin. Twin adds live data, layers and scenes on top of it.
midBody.open: The viewer runs in your browser; your file never leaves your computer.
